_what_this_is: Gaps a behaviour policy finds in a product: a rule it wants that the product cannot enforce or cannot express, who accepts the risk that leaves, and the request to the provider. Plus gaps found in our own behaviour policies and what was done about them. One file per entry under gaps/entries/; this index is generated from the files present.
how_to_add: Add one JSON file to data/gaps/entries/ with the fields listed in `fields`, by pull request to the repository or by sending the file to the editor. Every entry names who reported it and the evidence tier it rests on. No field is a score.
barrier_possible_values: boundary, if built outside the platform

entries.product: Google Calendar, the API and every connector built on it
entries.gap: Creating an event with guests sends the invitations at that moment: there is no draft, no preview and no edit before send, and the API's sendUpdates parameter only chooses who is notified.
entries.abp_impact: The rule draft only, a person sends cannot be expressed for calendar invitations at all. send.message.world through an invitation has no row a mandate can refuse while still granting the calendar.
entries.risk_to_accept: That the agent can invite anyone, immediately, with no step between composing and sending. Accepted by whoever grants a calendar to an agent, in the act of granting it.
entries.evidence: The Calendar API reference for events.insert and its sendUpdates parameter; the contributor's own agents, which hold Calendar.
entries.request: A draft or hold state for invitations, so that an event with guests can exist before anybody is notified.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.gap: Discarding a draft is irreversible and leaves no log the agent can read: a discarded draft cannot be recovered or audited through the connector.
entries.abp_impact: A mistaken discard is invisible to the deployer and to the agent's own end of turn report. Drafts are outside the grammar, so the loss cannot even be named as a row.
entries.risk_to_accept: That drafted work disappears without trace. Accepted by the deployer who lets the agent manage drafts.
entries.evidence: The connector's delete_draft tool, which the measured Gmail profile on this site lists on Needs approval; no untrash_draft exists among the thirty.
entries.request: A recoverable trash for drafts, and an audit event when one is discarded.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.gap: Image tags are stripped from drafts, so images can only go as attachments and inline images are impossible.
entries.abp_impact: None on the four objects. Recorded because it shapes what an agent can send, and a register that only lists what fails a policy would misstate what shapes one.
entries.risk_to_accept: None. A capability absent rather than a rule unenforceable.
entries.request: Inline images in HTML drafts, or a documented statement that they are stripped.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.gap: There is no raw MIME capture: an agent can read a message's content but cannot store the raw bytes, with full headers, DKIM signature and exact HTML.
entries.abp_impact: The provenance of stored mail is weaker than it should be. A record kept by the agent is a rendering, not the bytes, and cannot be re-verified against the sender's signature later.
entries.risk_to_accept: That a dispute over what a message said cannot be settled from the agent's copy. Accepted by whoever relies on that copy.
entries.evidence: The thirty connector tools as measured on this site; none returns raw MIME.
entries.request: A raw export the agent can write straight to storage.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.gap: Plain text drafts reach recipients with links rewritten through a google.com redirect, so the recipient sees a redirect URL rather than the address the agent wrote.
entries.abp_impact: None on the four objects. A fidelity and trust issue: a disclosed agent identity that sends links which look rewritten undercuts the disclosure.
entries.risk_to_accept: None. Workaround in use: an HTML body with explicit anchors.
entries.evidence: The contributor's sent mail, as received.
entries.request: Plain text links delivered as written, or the rewrite documented.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.product: Gmail, personal accounts and most Workspace editions
entries.gap: Personal Gmail has no native message encryption: only TLS in transit and Confidential Mode, which is not encryption. Hosted S/MIME and client side encryption exist on some Workspace editions only, and client side encryption leaves headers in clear.
entries.abp_impact: The rule only the recipient can read it cannot be enforced for most people. A hallucination, a bug or a wrong address leaks the whole message; nothing in the grant or the platform bounds send.message.world by who can open what was sent.
entries.barrier_possible: boundary, if built outside the platform
entries.risk_to_accept: That anything the agent sends can be read by whoever receives it, intended or not. Accepted by the deployer, until a key held by the recipient becomes the boundary.
entries.evidence: Google's own documentation of Confidential Mode, S/MIME and client side encryption and the editions each is available on; the contributor's edition.
entries.request: None of the provider. The contributor's answer is a browser extension that encrypts to a recipient's published key, which is a boundary the platform does not have to supply.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.product: Claude Cowork, and the account's connectors
entries.gap: A session's tools cannot be narrowed per agent. If the account holds Gmail write tools, every session on the account gets send and draft.
entries.abp_impact: The rule this agent may not send is an expectation with no barrier: the grant is the account's and the mandate is the agent's, and nothing in between can hold a difference.
entries.risk_to_accept: That every agent on the account can do whatever the widest one was given. Accepted by the account holder, in the act of enabling the connector.
entries.evidence: The contributor's own sessions. This site's estate case for three surfaces of one product records the same property as its first open question.
entries.request: Per agent or per session tool permissions, or an account level way to publish a narrower grant to a named agent.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.gap: Grants grow mid session. A newly added connector's tools appeared in a running session without anyone in the session asking for them.
entries.abp_impact: The reach changed while the mandate did not, and the grant the behaviour policy was written against is not the grant the session finished with. No object on this site has a row for a grant that moves during a session.
entries.risk_to_accept: That a session acquires capabilities nobody in it granted. Accepted by the account holder, who may not be in the session.
entries.evidence: The contributor's session, in which a Zapier connector's tools arrived mid session.
entries.request: A session pins its tool set at start, or is told, in the transcript, when the set changes.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.product: The sgit command line, versions 0.16.0 and 0.17.0
entries.gap: pull silently discards uncommitted edits to tracked files.
entries.abp_impact: An agent that writes to a vault and pulls before committing loses the write with no error. A record kept in a vault is only as durable as the agent's commit discipline.
entries.risk_to_accept: Lost edits. Workaround: commit before pull. Accepted by nobody; this one is a defect in our own estate and is reported.
entries.evidence: Reproduced by the contributor in a throwaway vault; report and script on request. This site's own session on 22 September cloned a vault with 0.16.0 and did not exercise pull.
entries.request: pull refuses, stashes, or merges when tracked files have uncommitted edits; a regression test.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.product: Every RiskMandate agent behaviour policy that grants Google Calendar
entries.gap: The calendar invitation gap (gap-001) is a gap in each of them: every one assumes a person releases outbound, and for invitations nothing can.
entries.abp_impact: send.message.world through an invitation sits on the wanted side wherever Calendar is granted, with no draft step to point a clause at.
entries.risk_to_accept: That an agent holding Calendar can invite anyone immediately.
entries.what_we_did: Recorded it here. The risk is accepted by the operator for every policy that grants Calendar, until a hold state exists or Calendar is withdrawn from the agents.
entries.evidence: gap-001, and the contributor's own policies.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.product: The Gmail connector on the agent's mailbox, as measured on 19 September 2026
entries.gap: send_message was on Always allow: the one irreversible action in the reach sat at nothing, while trashing a message needed approval.
entries.abp_impact: send.message.world at barrier none against a mandate that had never been elicited. The reach exceeded anything the business had said.
entries.risk_to_accept: That the agent sends to anyone with no prompt, and that a message which talks it into replying has a way out.
entries.what_we_did: The agent recommended moving send_message to Needs approval and leaving create_draft open. On the day the vault was written the change had not been made, so the risk was accepted by the operator, by reading each message as it was sent.
entries.evidence: GRANT.md and AGENTS.md in vault 02n7bz55, held verbatim on this site.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

entries.product: The same mailbox, the same session
entries.gap: Asked to move sixteen messages to a folder, the agent removed three from the inbox, since a move in Gmail is a label plus an INBOX removal. Nobody objected, and the agent's own reconstructed mandate then listed un-inboxing as authorised.
entries.abp_impact: A mandate line the business never granted, produced by an ambiguous instruction, a reasonable interpretation and no objection. The vault names it as the ratchet happening inside one session.
entries.risk_to_accept: That the inferred mandate drifts toward the reach with every action nobody objects to.
entries.what_we_did: Kept the mandate marked inferred, declined to compute a gap from it, and published the site's own starting mandate beside it on this site so the difference is a number. The business has not yet elicited the real one.
entries.evidence: MANDATE.md and DELTA.md in vault 02n7bz55; the two deltas on this site.
entries.reported_by: the RiskMandate.ai agent team, in a brief pack to this site dated 4 October 2026, pasted by the editor of record; self reported, not verified by this site

not_a_score: A count of open entries per provider is a count. It says nothing about whether any provider's product is acceptable for any deployment, because acceptability is not in this register.
